title: The interviewer's full internal brief — including submission-debrief red flags marked 'never say this aloud' — is returned to the candidate's browser by /connect, and ElevenLabs grounding rides on a client-side, tamperable prompt override
expected: Interviewer-internal material (probe plan, listen-fors, red flags) stays server-side; the candidate sees only the scrubbed run-of-show. The code states this intent itself: 'the followups' decision/red-flag notes are interviewer-internal and must never leak into the run-of-show the candidate sees' (interview-run.ts:87-90).
got: POST /api/interview/connect responds with both `instructions` and `groundedPrompt` in the JSON body for every session (connect/route.ts:172-179; groundedPrompt is non-null exactly for candidate mode, :167). The portal client calls /connect from the CANDIDATE's browser (VoiceInterview.tsx:524-537), so a candidate with devtools reads the entire brief. composeDebriefBrief embeds 'Internal red flag — never say this aloud: …' verbatim in that brief (interview-run.ts:107-110). For OpenAI the instructions are already delivered server-side at credential mint (openai.ts:92-109) — returning them to the browser is pure exposure; for ElevenLabs the brief is pushed as a client-side agent-prompt override (VoiceInterview.tsx:545-549), which also means the client controls what prompt the agent actually runs (an overrides-enabled agent accepts whatever the browser sends on the signed URL).
l2_priority: On a live candidate-token session, open devtools → Network → /connect and confirm instructions/groundedPrompt (incl. a red-flag line on a debrief entry) are in the response body; on an ElevenLabs session, attempt startSession with a modified override to confirm the agent accepts a candidate-authored prompt.
suggested_acceptance: /connect returns no interviewer-internal prompt material to candidate-mode browsers (OpenAI path needs neither field; ElevenLabs grounding moves server-side or to a server-mediated override), and red-flag notes never cross the trust boundary.

title: ScheduleTab's 'Spustit pohovor s AI' gives no delivery confirmation — it discards the API's delivered/revoked flags and opens the candidate's one-shot portal link in Petra's own browser tab
expected: After the action she sees what happened and to whom: 'link created for <candidate>, invite emailed (or NOT emailed), N prior links revoked' — the same feedback the pipeline drawer already gives (CandidateDrawer.tsx:819-827). Her scored criterion: no silent success.
got: startInterview() POSTs /api/interview/create and then only window.open(d.url) (ScheduleTab.tsx:145-166, :160). The response's `delivered`, `configured` and `revoked` fields (create/route.ts:111-121) are never rendered on this surface, so she cannot tell whether the candidate was actually invited or a prior link was killed. Worse, the tab she lands in IS the candidate's live single-use portal — if she ticks consent and talks, the session completes server-side (connect/route.ts:71-73) and the candidate's emailed link dies with 'already completed'.
l2_priority: Click the Schedule-tab button live: confirm no delivered/revoked feedback appears and that the opened tab is the candidate portal; confirm a recruiter-completed session 409s the candidate's copy of the link.
suggested_acceptance: The Schedule-tab action surfaces delivered/not-delivered + revoked-count feedback (parity with the drawer), and opening the candidate portal from the recruiter side is either explicit ('preview') or replaced by copy-link.

title: Agent grounding is 4/6: the brief carries real JD facts, CV-derived questions, match gaps and GitHub evidence — but no comp band and no prior pipeline context
expected: The agent knows what a senior screener would walk in with: the JD, this candidate's CV, what earlier stages already established, and the role's comp band (at minimum to deflect salary questions gracefully and not re-ask what screening already answered).
got: buildGroundedInterview grounds the brief in job title/company/seniority/location/workMode (interview-run.ts:138-142) plus the prep pack built from the real profile payload, job requirements, match scores/gaps and GitHub evidence (automation-run.ts:92,110,126-181; match_reasoning.py:50-95; automation.py:403-424). Missing: comp band/salary context (absent from reasoning_context and composeBrief) and prior pipeline history — screen verdict, recruiter notes, prior comms are never in the prep prompt. Score 4/6; candidate locale is only partially threaded (invite localized via entry.locale, create/route.ts:97; the session brief relies on the detect-and-follow prompt line, student-interview.ts:147-148).
l2_priority: In a live grounded session, ask the agent about salary and reference an earlier stage ('as I told the screening…') — observe whether it deflects gracefully or flounders; judge whether questions feel specific to THIS CV or only to the match summary.
suggested_acceptance: The brief includes a comp-band guardrail line (what to say when asked about salary) and a one-paragraph prior-stage recap, or the omission is documented as deliberate.

title: When prep generation fails, the created interview silently degrades to the generic ~5-minute quick screen — nothing tells Petra the link she just sent is ungrounded
expected: If the grounded brief could not be built, the recruiter is told ('generic screen — prep unavailable') before the invite goes out, or the create fails loudly.
got: buildGroundedInterview swallows a prep failure (catch at interview-run.ts:203-205) and falls back to composeBrief-with-empty-chronology → defaultInterviewerInstructions + QUICK_SCREEN_MIN (interview-run.ts:50, :212-215). The create response carries no grounded/generic indicator (create/route.ts:111-121); the only visible clue is the duration (5 vs ~20 min). Honest toward the candidate (truthful short duration), silent toward the recruiter.
l2_priority: Create a link for an entry with no profile/prep and CLI unavailable: confirm the UI gives no ungrounded warning and the portal shows ~5 min.
suggested_acceptance: The create response includes grounded:true/false and both recruiter surfaces render a visible 'generic screen' warning when false.

title: AI scorecard prose (summary, evidence framing) carries no locale directive — a Czech recruiter likely reads an English headline verdict; only the rubric labels are localized
expected: Her scored criterion: generated reasoning renders correctly in Czech; English-only headline output is a finding.
got: Only the `prep` task receives --lang (automation-run.ts:170-172); the scorecard prompt has no language_directive (pipeline/jobfit/automation.py:557-587 builds the rubric prompt with none). The transcript-quoted evidence will be Czech when the call was Czech, but the model-authored summary/recommendation prose is language-undirected. The modal localizes competency labels client-side (InterviewTranscriptModal.tsx:88, rubricLabel(competency, locale)) — partial mitigation.
l2_priority: Complete a Czech-language screen live and read the AI scorecard: is the summary in Czech or English? If English on a cs workspace, confirm severity (her criterion makes an English headline a finding).
suggested_acceptance: The scorecard synthesis receives the workspace/entry locale and its summary renders in the recruiter's language.

title: The review surface is evidence-anchored end to end: scorecard quotes click-jump to the exact transcript turn, human and AI scorecards are visually distinct, failed calls are never scored, and the verdict is sealed with its model version
expected: A transcript + usable result she can defend to a manager — not raw audio to re-listen.
got: findEvidenceTurn anchors each rating's quote to a transcript turn with a distinctive-word majority guard so paraphrases aren't mis-anchored (InterviewTranscriptModal.tsx:46-68); anchored quotes are clickable jump-to-moment buttons and cited turns are badged (:216-244, :263). The human scorecard renders coral-tinted so the two are never confused (:110-132). Upstream honesty: only a live, ≥1-turn, error-free call is 'completed' (finalize-status.ts:34-37); a failed call's transcript is never scored and never sets the Interview→Offer approval (complete/route.ts:150-159); the transcript persists BEFORE scoring so no phantom gate approval can exist (:118-134); transcript truncation is logged, not silent (interview-run.ts:258-265); the AI verdict is sealed as a decision record with the scorecard prompt version as actor (:168-179).
ceiling: Evidence anchoring is lexical (word-overlap), so a heavily paraphrased quote renders unanchored rather than linked; scorecard quality itself is model-dependent and only L2 can judge it against her senior bar.
l2_priority: On a real completed session, click 2-3 evidence quotes and confirm each lands on the correct turn; check one deliberately paraphrased quote renders unanchored, not wrongly anchored.
suggested_acceptance: Every rating with evidence either jumps to its true source turn or renders as plain text — never to an unrelated turn.

title: Link lifecycle is single-live-link with a mid-call guard: reissue revokes prior links, a live call refuses reissue (409 + non-interactive pill), terminal entries revoke on sight, and voice minutes are billing-gated for the whole booked call
expected: She can't accidentally torpedo a running interview, double-invite a candidate, or run an unfunded call.
got: create revokes open sessions first so exactly one link is live (create/route.ts:63-69), refuses while a recently-touched in_progress session exists unless force (:53-61); ScheduleTab renders the live state as a status pill, not a re-runnable button (ScheduleTab.tsx:294-308) and explains the 409 in Czech (:158, messages/cs.json:1657). connect enforces single-use after completion (connect/route.ts:71-73), revoked/expired refusal from the shared expiry authority (:84-92; db/interviews.ts:203-212), revoke-on-sight for terminal entries (:93-99), and a per-token connect throttle (:112-114). The meter gate books the whole call, not one leftover minute (create/route.ts:30-31); minutes debit idempotently on the applied completion only (complete/route.ts:143-148).
ceiling: The live-call recency window can still classify a zombie connect as live for its duration, delaying a legitimate reissue until it ages out (or force is used).
l2_priority: Confirm live that a second 'Spustit pohovor' during an active call is refused with the localized explanation, and that a reissue after completion revokes the old link.
suggested_acceptance: At any moment at most one usable link exists per entry, and no recruiter action can kill a call that is actually in progress without an explicit override.

title: Every lifecycle state she can meet renders an honest card — completed, revoked, expired — the shown duration is the session's real run-of-show length, and a dropped call keeps her link retryable instead of locking her out
expected: An honest 'completed / a human reviews this' close, never a dead Start button; the stated length is the real one.
got: Completed → closed thank-you card (page.tsx:26-33, cs.json:761-762); revoked/expired → honest inactive card (page.tsx:39-46) using the single expiry authority shared with the credential gate (db/interviews.ts:203-212) so page and API can never disagree. Duration comes from session.durationMin with a documented grounded default (page.tsx:24, :58; interview-duration.mjs:25-44 — the provider cap clears the grounded maximum so a real 20-30 min interview is never severed). In-client, a completed ending swaps controls for the same closing card the server renders (VoiceInterview.tsx:674-681) while a failed ending (zero-turn, error blip, never-live) keeps retry (finalize-status.ts:34-37; VoiceInterview.tsx:102-108); her answers survive a tab close via sendBeacon persisted as 'failed', never scored (VoiceInterview.tsx:372-387; complete/route.ts:150-159), and a save failure is told to her (VoiceInterview.tsx:278-281, cs.json:794).
ceiling: The closing card promises 'the recruiter will get back to you' but the portal offers no status link back into /status/[token] — she leaves the page with a promise, not a place to check it.
l2_priority: Confirm live: completed link reload shows the closed card; a mid-call tab close then reopen lets her retry; the header duration matches the agenda chip and the invite email's stated length.
suggested_acceptance: No state of /interview/[token] ever shows a Start button that cannot work, and the stated duration equals the session's stored run-of-show length.

title: AI disclosure + consent clear her bar: plain-Czech, unticked, refusable, enforced server-side at both credential-mint and transcript-persist, with a truthful 'human decides' claim and a jurisdiction-aware disclosure
expected: Know if/how AI is used on her and consent in language she gets, before AI touches her, with no dark pattern.
got: The consent copy states AI-led, transcribed for a human reviewer, no audio stored, in idiomatic Czech (cs.json:787) and the checkbox defaults to unticked (VoiceInterview.tsx:90). It is not a UI convention: /connect 403s a candidate session without literal consent===true BEFORE any provider credential is minted (connect/route.ts:149-155; interview-consent.ts:49-51) and /complete refuses to persist a candidate transcript without consent_at recorded (complete/route.ts:63-70; interview-consent.ts:56-58). The no-audio claim matches the persistence path (transcript turns only, complete/route.ts:77-102). The 'human reviews' chips (page.tsx:60-66) are truthful: the scorecard sets a scorecard_review approval feeding a human Decisions gate, never an auto-advance (complete/route.ts:150-179). AiDisclosure resolves the workspace's compliance regime and names its framework + data law (AiDisclosure.tsx:30-45, :57-59).
ceiling: Consent is refusable but refusal has no onward path (see vi-tereza-consent-decline-deadend); and consent is bundled — she cannot consent to the interview while objecting to any single element (transcription is inherent to the design).
l2_priority: Render the portal in cs and confirm the disclosure/consent reads as plain language on a phone; verify a no-consent direct POST to /connect really 403s.
suggested_acceptance: No candidate call can start or persist without explicit recorded consent, and the disclosure renders in the candidate's language.

title: The call path anticipates her real environment: preflight names webview/HTTP/WebRTC root causes before dialing, the mic-permission wait is explained, and a hung connect errors honestly at 30s
expected: A first-round screen on her phone that doesn't strand her on a frozen 'Connecting…'.
got: voicePreflightError diagnoses insecure context, in-app webview (no mediaDevices), and missing WebRTC in root-cause order BEFORE any /connect call burns credentials (preflight.ts:46-56; VoiceInterview.tsx:488-493). While the OS mic prompt is open she sees 'the wait is on you' guidance (VoiceInterview.tsx:99-102, :781). A connect that isn't live in 30s becomes an explicit error, never a hang (:510-522), and a late provider connect after timeout is abandoned rather than presented as a live call whose transcript could never persist (:300-311).
ceiling: The preflight messages themselves are English-only (vi-tereza-preflight-error-english), and preflight cannot detect a muted/broken mic — that still surfaces as a zero-turn failed call.
l2_priority: Real latency is the L2 question: voice connect + turn-taking on a phone-class network; confirm no premature client timeout during a normal 15-130s AI-surface window.
suggested_acceptance: A doomed environment is told exactly what to do before dialing; a viable one reaches live within the timeout or gets an honest, retryable error.

title: Her entry premise — 'I got a link' — is environment-gated twice: invite delivery is a local Outbox simulation unless COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL is set, and the local token-mint fixture is still an open env question
expected: The freshly minted interview link lands in her inbox, in her language, so the journey can start at all.
got: Delivery machinery exists and is ship-shaped: dispatchInterviewInvite routes through the durable Outbox channel with audit log + dead-letter, localized from the entry's locale, with an absolute link (comms-dispatch.ts:395-416; create/route.ts:91-109), and delivery is gated on the provider being configured so she's never invited to a dead link (:92). But the channel is a real relay ONLY when COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL is set (comms.ts:36, :98) — default is a local Outbox her inbox never sees; the recruiter copy-link is the manual fallback. Separately, uat/env.md open question #3 (env.md:127-133, :139-140) means no local path to mint her token fixture is recorded — until resolved her whole journey is unreachable at L2, not failing.
scope_note: Demo/case scope: the durable Outbox with dead-letters IS the designed local behavior; a real relay is a deployment concern. Suppressed as a defect only to that extent — the fixture gap remains the #1 L2 blocker for her.
l2_priority: Resolve the mint path (create a session via POST /api/interview/create on a seeded entry and capture the returned token); verify the Outbox entry contains the absolute /interview/<token> link in cs and that the link opens the portal.
suggested_acceptance: env.md records a one-command token mint; the Outbox invite for a cs entry contains a working absolute link and Czech copy.

title: Declining the AI-interview consent is a silent dead end — the portal offers no alternative path (human interview request, contact) for a candidate who refuses
expected: Consent that is 'genuinely refusable' includes an onward step for refusal: a way to say 'I'd rather talk to a person' or at least a contact — otherwise refusing costs her the opportunity, which pressures the consent.
got: The portal renders only the agenda sidebar, the voice client and the disclosure (page.tsx:48-85); with the checkbox unticked, Start stays disabled (VoiceInterview.tsx:709-717) and nothing else is offered — no contact affordance, no 'request a human-led round', no explanation of what refusing means for her application. The consent itself is clean (unticked, plain Czech, server-enforced), so this is a missing next step, not a dark pattern.
l2_priority: Confirm live that a non-consenting candidate has no onward affordance; check whether any comm (the invite email) names an alternative or contact she could use instead.
suggested_acceptance: The portal (or the invite) offers a refusal path — contact the recruiter / request a human interview — so consent is free in substance, not only in form.

title: The preflight error messages — covering what the code itself calls the single most common real-world failure (email-app webview) — are hardcoded English on an otherwise fully Czech portal
expected: The recovery instruction for a blocked mic/webview open renders in her language; she taps the emailed link in her mail app in the evening — exactly the webview scenario.
got: voicePreflightError returns hardcoded English strings for insecure-context, webview/no-mediaDevices, and no-WebRTC (preflight.ts:47-55); VoiceInterview surfaces them verbatim via setError (VoiceInterview.tsx:488-493, rendered :740-744). Every other portal string is localized (messages/cs.json:760-816). A Czech retail candidate stuck in Gmail's preview gets instructions she may not be able to read, on the most likely failure path of the whole journey (the invite arrives by email).
l2_priority: Open the portal in a simulated webview/insecure context with a cs locale: confirm the English message renders. If the emailed-link → mobile-webview open proves to be the default path, raise to major (it blocks completion with an unreadable instruction).
suggested_acceptance: Preflight errors are next-intl keys rendered in the candidate's locale, matching the rest of the portal.

title: Czech is never configured at the provider — the portal's cs language hint is dropped by both adapters, so the agent's opening (which by brief comes BEFORE she speaks) may land in English
expected: A Czech candidate's session opens in Czech. The brief instructs the agent to introduce itself first (interview-run.ts:62), so detect-and-follow (student-interview.ts:147-148) cannot resolve the language before that opening.
got: The portal seeds language from her UI locale (VoiceInterview.tsx:95-97) and sends it to /connect (:527-532), which passes it to adapter.connect (connect/route.ts:164) — but the OpenAI adapter destructures only `instructions` and never configures language (openai.ts:92-109), and the ElevenLabs adapter's connect() takes no arguments at all (elevenlabs.ts:19-35); the browser override carries only the prompt, no language override (VoiceInterview.tsx:545-549). Spoken language therefore rides entirely on the PERSONA_LANGUAGE_DETECT prompt line and (for EL) the dashboard agent's configuration.
l2_priority: Start a cs candidate session on each provider and assert the agent's FIRST sentence is Czech; if it opens in English before she speaks, this is the jarring first impression her senior bar rejects — raise accordingly.
suggested_acceptance: The session's stored/hinted language reaches the provider config (OpenAI session field / EL language override), and a cs session verifiably opens in Czech.
